answer: An attacker can mint identities in bulk, but cannot be in many live conversations at once. At unpredictable moments the network opens a ninety-second simultaneity window: every claiming agent must sustain a distinct interactive stream, answering changing prompts with a steady pulse of replies whose timing and content diverge per agent. One operator puppeteering a hundred shells fails, because attention cannot be split that thin in real time, and yesterday's transcript is a relic, useless as shale dust for replay. Cost scales with concurrent presence, not reusable capital.
